advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that resolves an alias shared by two ticket dirs through the prebuilt alias_index and asserts it returns None (ambiguous), matching _scan_alias.
evidence: src/rebar/_ids.py:334-349: `alias_matches = (alias_index.get(ticket_id, []) if alias_index is not None else _scan_alias(...))` then `if len(alias_matches) > 1: ... return None`
Docstring claim src/rebar/_ids.py:284-285: 'The result is identical to per-call scanning (same match set, same ambiguity handling).'

tests/unit/test_referencing_commits_alias_scan_perf.py builds only distinct single-match aliases (`decoy_aliases = [_new_ticket_alias(...) for i in range(6)]`), so the indexed >1-match ambiguity branch is never driven.
src/rebar/_ids.py:334-338: `if alias_index is not None else _scan_alias(ticket_id, tracker_dir)`
src/rebar/_ids.py:229-233: build_alias_index returns None on OSError listing the tracker
src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:194-199 comment: '`None` (tracker unreadable) falls back to per-call scanning, preserving behavior.'
tests/unit/test_referencing_commits_alias_scan_perf.py uses a normal readable tracker, so build_alias_index never returns None and the fallback branch is not exercised.
advisory.finding: The newly-added indexed alias-resolution path (alias_index.get returning a multi-element list) has no test, though the resolver docstring contracts 'same ambiguity handling' as per-call scanning. When two ticket directories share one effective alias, build_alias_index groups both names under that alias and resolve_ticket_id must hit the len(alias_matches) > 1 branch and return None; the new test only exercises distinct single-match aliases.
merged_from: The newly-added None-fallback branch in resolve_ticket_id (`else _scan_alias(...)` when alias_index is None) is untested. commit_impact.referencing_commits passes build_alias_index(tracker), which returns None on an OSError listing the tracker; the resolver must then fall back to per-call scanning ('preserving behavior' per the added comment). The new test always supplies a readable tracker, so this fallback never executes.
scenarios: A store where two ticket dirs resolve to the same effective alias and that alias appears as a historical commit trailer during a close precheck.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 156 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 4234-821b-150c-461b has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 4234-821b-150c-461b` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 4234-821b-150c-461b` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 4234-821b-150c-461b --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
